name: IconButton
description: Icon-only action button. Wraps @dt/Button in its rounded icon-only form with an enforced accessible label, sharing Button's variant (weight) x tone (semantic) matrix and surface awareness.

ariaRequirements: `label` prop is required and renders as the accessible name; the icon glyph itself is `aria-hidden`.
`tooltip` is hover-only garnish; it never replaces `label` as the accessible name.
Disabled state forwards `aria-disabled` and removes pointer events; focus remains routable so keyboard users can discover the disabled affordance.
a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-07-05 — beta→stable (fleet #11): re-verified independently. Delegates all styling to stable @dt/Button, so reduced-motion (Button.module.css prefers-reduced-motion guard), variant/tone/surface matrix, and forced-colors inherit from Button. axe + plays green on all 9 stories in light/dark/forced-colors; 100% controls operable, 0 inert; AT snapshots captured for the four beta-matrix stories in all four modes. 2026-07-03 origin: API aligned to platinum variant x tone conventions (ghost/outline/default removed), keyboard/ARIA contract reviewed, axe unit tests added.

dense: icon-only action button; wraps Button (rounded) so variant (weight) x tone x surface stay in lockstep, sm/md/lg, required accessible label, tooltip passthrough

usage.description: IconButton is an icon-only action for compact surfaces: toolbars, card corners, table rows, dialog close affordances. It wraps Button in its rounded icon-only form, so weight, tone, and surface behave exactly like Button; label is required and becomes the accessible name.

bestPractices.description: Write label as the action, like Close dialog or Copy link, never the icon name like X or Clipboard.
Stay on the default variant=tertiary in toolbars and chrome; reserve primary for the one dominant action of a compact surface.
Pick an icon whose meaning survives without text (x, magnifying-glass, caret-*); if you have to explain the icon, use Button with a visible label instead.
Add tooltip for sighted-user reassurance on ambiguous glyphs; the label still carries the accessible name.
Use surface=onDark or onBrand when the control sits on a dark or brand band instead of overriding colors.
Do not omit or auto-generate label; there is no fallback announcement and axe fails the render.
Do not use IconButton for primary marketing CTAs; text plus icon is more discoverable, use Button with an icon prop.
Do not stack more than about five icon-only actions in a row without grouping or labels; recognition drops sharply.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: The glyph, passed as an element or a Phosphor icon name string; always aria-hidden.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Invisible accessible name (aria-label) announcing the action to assistive tech.

anatomy.name: Tooltip
anatomy.description: Native hover tooltip for sighted users; never the accessible name.

icon.description: Icon glyph: a rendered element (e.g. <CaretRight />) or a Phosphor icon name (e.g. "x").

label.description: Accessible name when `aria-labelledby` is not set

surface.description: Surface the control sits on; prefer over color overrides on tinted bands.

tooltip.description: Native tooltip text shown on hover; the `label` stays the accessible name.

forbiddenUse: Omit `label` — there is no fallback announcement.
Use for primary marketing CTAs — text + icon is more discoverable; use `Button` with an icon prop.
Rely on `tooltip` as the only accessible name.
prefersOver: raw button with an svg child
Button with accessibleName for icon-only cases
